key_insight: Frozen visual world models for Atari Pong often fail at task-critical dynamics like tracking the ball, and concept-guided spatial regularization can partially improve them.
engineering_relevance: For model-based RL systems, evaluating the world model in isolation is essential because strong agent scores can hide poor predictive fidelity that harms downstream policy learning.
method: Reproduced five visual world-model agents: DreamerV3, DIAMOND, TWISTER, Simulus, and STORM.
Ran closed-loop rollout diagnostics using separately trained policies interacting with frozen world models.
Added Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization (CGSReg), a segmented-region reconstruction loss, and tested its effect on rollouts and zero-shot pixel-space MBRL.
evidence_signal: Across all five models, rollouts showed errors such as ball disappearance and incorrect ball-paddle interactions, and zero-shot policies trained inside frozen models underperformed the original pipelines, with DreamerV3 dropping from -5.5 to -20.9 mean return.
watch_item: CGSReg improves some models and metrics but does not fully resolve world-model bottlenecks, so results may depend on architecture and evaluation setting.
paper_title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong
